## SECTION E: PRINCIPLES (E1-E16)

| # | Principle | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| E1 | Quick wins | Progress early → stay longer, complete more, refer more. Dopamine loop. |
| E2 | 3rd-5th grade language | Confusion = dropout. Simplicity = confidence = execution. |
| E3 | Checklists everywhere | Removes thinking/ambiguity. Creates measurable progress. |
| E4 | WHY/WHAT/HOW/DO NOT/ACTION | WHY=buy-in, WHAT=understanding, HOW=execution, DO NOT=prevents mistakes, ACTION=results. |
| E5 | Gate hard before core | Unready clients executing = bad results/refunds/reviews. |
| E6 | Celebrate relentlessly | Emotional anchors prevent dropout at predictable doubt moments. |
| E7 | Document everything | Guarantee trail + accountability + testimonial proof. |
| E8 | DFY visible but locked | Intrigue/desire/natural upsell without being pushy. |
| E9 | Shorter lessons (1-10 min) | Lower barrier, higher completion, more frequent wins. |
| E10 | Confirm-suggest-cycle | Prevents building wrong. Catches optimizations in real-time. |
| E11 | Zones of proximal development | Push just beyond ability. Not so hard it overwhelms. (Vygotsky/Sarah Turner) |
| E12 | 6 adult learning principles | Know WHY before HOW. Practical/relevant/problem-solving/intrinsic motivation. (Sarah Turner) |
| E13 | MVP first, expand later | Launch 7DFS + Foundation first. Film later with real data. (Sarah Turner) |
| E14 | Compounding actions (30 min/day) | Consistent small actions beat marathon sessions. |
| E15 | Community > course for retention | Seed engagement from Module 1.1. Wednesday Wins, peer support. (Sarah Turner) |
| E16 | Challenges as engagement drivers | Periodic live challenges increase completion + social proof. (Sarah Turner) |

## SECTION F: CLIENT EXPERIENCE TARGETS (F1-F10)

| # | Target | How |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Quick wins | First win within 30 min. Win in every module. |
| F2 | Highest probability of success | Gate hard. Clear roadmaps. Don't let unready execute. |
| F3 | Maximum clarity | No jargon without explanation. Checklists. Visual roadmaps. |
| F4 | Simplicity | Fewer classrooms. Shorter lessons. One concept per lesson. |
| F5 | Ease / effortlessness | Tell exactly what to do, in what order, with what words. |
| F6 | Remove heavy lifting | Templates, scripts, sequences, checklists, DFY option. |

| F9 | Tangible actionable roadmap | Program → classroom → module → daily. All integrated. |
| F10 | Unreasonable not to succeed | Complete every checklist = near-impossible to fail. |

## SECTION H: OPTIMIZATION CYCLE

**The Protocol:**
1. Alan confirms any deliverable
2. Builder provides optimization suggestions with specific reasoning
3. Alan reviews — confirms, adjusts, or rejects each
4. Builder incorporates changes, presents updated version
5. Repeat 2-4 until Alan confirms no more improvements
6. ONLY THEN move to next step. Builder presents options, Alan picks.

**Applies to:** Everything. No exceptions. Classroom maps, module lists, lesson lists, roadmaps, templates, checklists, architecture maps, outlines, audits. The SOP itself.

**Label:** `OPTIMIZATION CYCLE — Round [#]`

## SECTION I: SARAH TURNER IMPROVEMENTS (I1-I10)

| # | Improvement | Why It Matters |
|---|---|---|
| I1 | Pre-program survey (goals, experience, expectations) | Personalizes Day 1. Go/No-Go captures credit but NOT goals. |
| I2 | Wednesday Wins (weekly win-sharing) | Compounding social proof. Retention. |
| I3 | Challenges (30-Day Credit Cleanup, 7DFS Sprint) | Massively increases completion. Group accountability. |
| I4 | Weekly digest pulling students back | Combats #1 problem: not logging in. |
| I5 | Learning objective per lesson: "By end, you will have [done X]" | Measurable completion = satisfaction. |
| I6 | Multiple learning styles (video + PDF + workbook + community) | All 4 styles = max retention. |
| I7 | Reconnect to WHY at multiple points | Students drift. Prompts reactivate motivation. |
| I8 | Goal-setting at start with "first level of success" (CRITICAL) | Prevents mismatched expectations = disappointment. |
| I9 | Giveaways/prizes for engagement | Gamification. Low cost, high engagement. |
| I10 | Track and share student data obsessively | Marketing, validation, stuck-points, testimonials. |

## QUICK REFERENCE CARD

### Before Delivering ANY Output (POVP — D19)
1. Identify relevant prompts from Section J
2. Read each one WORD-BY-WORD (do not skim)
3. Compare to your output for exact match
4. Flag mismatches. Fix before delivering.
5. Display the checked-off list in the output (D20)

### Before Ending ANY Response (PFV — D21)
1. Did I enter the optimization cycle with suggestions?
2. Did I label it OPTIMIZATION CYCLE — Round [#]?
3. Did I skip any build steps? (check Build Position)
4. After cycle completes: did I present next step options?

### Content Rules (Every Output)
- D1: One step at a time. Never combine.
- D6: Never assume. If unclear, ask.
- D7: 5th grader simplicity filter.
- D22: SOP is a deliverable. Full treatment.
- A29: Classroom 3 = REQUIRED. Internal skip logic only.
- A30: 1-5 required. 6-7-8 optional.
- A38: START/END with real-time checklist.
- D23: Every update = new version number.
- D24: State BOTH current and proposed versions.

### The Cycle (Section H — Every Deliverable)
Alan confirms → Suggestions with reasoning → Alan reviews → Incorporate → Repeat until no improvements → Present next options → Alan picks.
